BMI for women: useful context for adult health

BMI categories are shared across adult sexes, while life stage, hormones, body composition, and personal history still matter.

Written by Elena Morris, CHCW · Medically reviewed by Dr. Daniel Chen, MD · Updated July 24, 2026

Answer: The standard adult BMI scale is the same for women and men. It should not be used to assess pregnancy, and it cannot measure body fat directly.

Life stage changes the picture

Pregnancy requires pregnancy-specific care rather than an adult BMI target. Menopause can affect body composition and waist distribution. These changes are normal reasons to seek individualized, non-judgmental guidance.

Beyond the scale

Strength, energy, sleep, blood pressure, blood sugar, and emotional wellbeing can all be meaningful signs of health. Talk with a clinician about any unexplained change in weight or appetite.
